import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    # using Welch's t-test for each feature
    significant_features = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
            # For clinical features, use Mann-Whitney U test
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            try:
                t_stat, p_val = stats.mannwhitneyu(y0, y1, alternative='two-sided')
            except:
                continue
        else:
            # For expression/copy_number, use Welch's t-test
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
            
        if p_val < 0.05:
            # Calculate effect size (mean difference)
            mean_diff = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
            significant_features.append((fid, abs(mean_diff), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (descending)
    significant_features.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Check for near-duplicates (correlated features)
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                fid1, fid2 = feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]
                # Add pair in canonical order to avoid duplicates
                pair = tuple(sorted([fid1, fid2]))
                correlated_pairs.add(pair)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates, keeping the one with highest effect size
    unique_features = set()
    for fid, effect_size, p_val in significant_features:
        # Check if this feature is correlated with any already selected feature
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in unique_features:
            pair = tuple(sorted([fid, selected_fid]))
            if pair in correlated_pairs:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            unique_features.add(fid)
    
    # If we have too many features, limit to top ones
    drivers = tuple(list(unique_features)[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Check stratum consistency
    if len(drivers) > 0:
        # Fit logistic regression in each stratum and check consistency
        strata_consistent = True
        for stratum in set(feats.stratum):
            mask = np.array(feats.stratum) == stratum
            stratum_x = feats.x[mask]
            stratum_y = feats.y[mask]
            if len(np.unique(stratum_y)) < 2:
                continue  # Skip strata with only one outcome class
                
            # Use all features for this stratum
            model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=1.0)
            try:
                model.fit(stratum_x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in drivers]], stratum_y)
                # Check if coefficients are non-zero for at least one driver
                if not any(abs(coef) > 1e-6 for coef in model.coef_[0]):
                    strata_consistent = False
                    break
            except:
                strata_consistent = False
                break
        
        if not strata_consistent:
            drivers = ()
    
    # For the regression, include all features that are drivers
    columns = drivers
    
    # No interaction terms (products) needed for this case
    products = ()
    
    # Create loadings dictionary (simple sum of standardized features)
    loadings = {}
    for fid in drivers:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        loadings[fid] = 1.0  # Equal weights for simplicity
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed maximum drivers
    if len(drivers) > 4:
        drivers = drivers[:4]
        columns = columns[:4]
        
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
